f2.interpretation: F2 obtains no hidden benefit from crossing a window boundary; full window depths are even and odd tails remain token local.

ceil_and_boundary_attack.conclusion: The sealed F4/F8 counts charge each window separately and are not contaminated by an illegal cross-window or cross-token ceil.

baseline_fairness.admission: Only the decomposition is fair enough for architectural screening. The combined 1.09655x point changes source bandwidth and is not a matched physical speedup.

precompacted_oracle_attack.finding: The published 192 ingress bits/cycle describe two already-compacted descriptors, not the raw bitmap input. A four-beat scanner has only thin average headroom and still must survive sparse bursts, window tails and stalls.

hammer_findings.finding: The sealed manifest is internally valid and pins the analyzer, contract, result, README, prior M196 review and unchanged docs/359.
An independently authored decoder and scheduler reproduce every F={1,2,4,8}, B={2,3,4} aggregate wall count and every published per-stage count exactly; the four M196 F1 crosschecks also close.
Packing is charged as ceil(entries/F) separately for each window. The independent illegal-copack attack confirms that F4/F8 did not borrow tail capacity across windows or tokens.

The F2/B2 selection is a sensible smallest-width screen: 1.096550x combines 1.056447x packing with only 1.037961x pair-fusion increment versus the iso-width W1 baseline. The contract and README correctly withhold RTL, physical, FC2, FFN and system claims.

The producer is a preindexed nonzero oracle. At 51.7253% descriptor density, sustaining two nonzeros per cycle requires 3.8666 raw 96-bit beats per cycle on average, so the advertised 192-bit descriptor interface does not account for the approximately 384-bit raw scanner, zero rejection, stable compaction or burst buffering.

No executable frontend proves descriptor conservation and monotonically increasing beat order across two-lane output, per-window close, zero-token flush, odd tails and arbitrary output backpressure. F2 cannot be admitted until that source schedule is cycle-charged on all frozen payloads.

The finite queue, accepted head advancement, SRAM request/response tags, stale-response quarantine, result stalls and Acc24/commit path remain outside the recurrence. Absolute counts are exact only for the sealed abstract schedule.

The field ingress_bits_per_cycle should be labeled compacted_descriptor_bits_per_cycle. A matched comparison must hold raw scan bandwidth, write ports, buffer bits and scanner/compactor area/timing/energy constant.
F4/F8 gains are diminishing before charging wider scan/compact networks, and their large per-window padding makes them poor immediate RTL targets; retaining F2 is reasonable.

p0_before_f2_speedup_admission: Build a raw-bitmap, at-least-four-beat scanner plus stable two-lane compactor and rerun all 120 payloads while charging zeros, token/window tails, bubbles and arbitrary downstream stalls.
Prove bit-exact descriptor conservation, source beat order, token/window identity, no cross-window packing and exactly-once tail release under backpressure.
Integrate the F2 producer with the two-window finite queue, accepted head advancement, SRAM request/response tags, epoch stale-response quarantine and Acc24/commit retirement.
Run matched Synopsys VCS and DC/STA, then report throughput/area and energy against an equal raw-scanner-bandwidth W1 baseline.
p1_for_complete_fc2: Rename the 192-bit rate as compacted descriptor output bandwidth and state the raw scan width separately.
Pin an edge-accurate runner receipt and include measured SRAM latency, response arbitration and output backpressure in the payload replay.
Charge buffer macros, scanner/compactor wires and ports, BN2/residual/ATLIF commit, final-token drain and token header/done cycles.
